source.title: Statistical Knowledge Assessment for Large Language Models
source.authors: Qingxiu Dong; Jingjing Xu; Lingpeng Kong; Zhifang Sui; Lei Li

record.tranche_reason: It measures factual-knowledge generation across model sizes, a different measure from downstream-task benchmarks or pretraining loss, and reports a scaling result relevant to V6.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out cross-entropy, training tokens, training compute, or a compute-optimal allocation. Its KaRR measure assesses reliable factual-knowledge generation; the scale-related findings are recorded under V6. The paper also reports prompt-variance and spurious-correlation analyses, but these do not measure any claim version.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a knowledge-assessment method paper. It still scores 20 LLMs of different sizes with KaRR, and its within-family size comparisons bear on V6 in a new setting: reliable factual-knowledge generation. Those comparisons are LLaMA 7B/13B/65B, T5-large vs T5-3B, and OPT 350M/2.7B/175B. There is no loss, power-law fit or extrapolation, so it is T3, not T2.
record.authors_conclusion: The main conclusion concerns the method: KaRR correlates with human judgement (Kendall's τ 0.43) and has low prompt variance and spurious correlation. As a secondary finding, the authors say knowledge within the same backbone follows the scaling law, with benefits varying across models. They also say instruction tuning (Alpaca) can harm reliable factual generation, while tuning on data from a stronger model (Vicuna) can help. The record's paraphrase is right but omits that the scale result is secondary.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures thresholded factual-knowledge generation using KaRR, not held-out cross-entropy or loss-versus-parameter/token/compute curves.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that relation-prompt choice changes the variance of several assessment methods; KaRR has variance 0.67 and standard deviation 0.82 across paraphrased templates. Its sampling parameter K also affects assessment variance and correlation with human evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed 13B size, LLaMA-derived tunings shift KaRR widely: Alpaca 8.24, LLaMA 13.86, WizardLM 16.90, Vicuna 19.50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training (instruction tuning or distillation) can move factual-knowledge reliability more than a several-fold change in parameter count.

record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The study does not measure pretraining loss, tokens, compute, or fitted scaling exponents. Its scale analysis is limited to selected model families and relations; Figure 5's plotted values are not stated in the text. Overall KaRR scores depend on a threshold aligned using human judgments on a sampled set.

untested.parts: All of it: no pretraining loss is measured.
All of it: no fits and no extrapolation.
All of it: no compute or token allocation.
All of it: no shape ablation at fixed size.
Whether the improvement is predictable (no functional fit, no prediction of larger models), its relation to pretraining loss, and general downstream benchmarks.

missing.what: Scaling series the authors describe: T5-small→T5-3B, plus GPT2 and OPT benefiting 'to a lesser extent'. The small T5, GPT2 and OPT sizes are not in Table 2, and the cited 'Fig. 2' is a method illustration.
Claim that below 1B, GPT2 and OPT significantly outperform T5. No numbers are given.

record.verdict_notes: 'Scaling law' here means only a monotonic size trend in a thresholded proportion: the threshold of 22 was calibrated on GPT2-XL. No power-law form is fitted. The Vicuna size is inconsistent in the paper (7B in the appendix, 13B in the table), and the LLaMA2 '65B' entry is likely 70B. The section 4 intro says 14 LLMs, while elsewhere the paper says 20.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power-law fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architectural details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study assesses factual-knowledge generation, not general downstream-task performance or a relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
Sensitivity of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation to fitting choices, and departures of loss curves from a power law.

relationships.condition: Within a model family (LLaMA 7B/13B/65B; T5-large→T5-3B; OPT 350M/2.7B/175B)
relationships.reason: KaRR rises with size in every within-family series: LLaMA 12.37→13.86→14.56 and T5 3.22→9.52. For OPT, the authors report larger models better on more relations (r10, r13, r18, r03, r07, r21–r26).
relationships.display_finding: KaRR increased through 12.37, 13.86, and 14.56 for LLaMA and from 3.22 to 9.52 for T5, while larger OPT models performed better on more relations.

relationships.condition: Across model families, and in the size of the gain within families
relationships.reason: Across families, size does not order KaRR: GLM-10B scores 5.59 and Falcon-7B 7.97, below GPT2-XL-1.56B at 12.27 and GPT-NEO-2.65B at 13.44. Within families the gain ranges from about 3x for T5 to under 20% for LLaMA over 9x (r01, r05, r06, r08, r09, r11, r10, r18, r03, r07).
relationships.display_finding: GLM-10B and Falcon-7B scored 5.59 and 7.97, below GPT2-XL-1.56B at 12.27 and GPT-NEO-2.65B at 13.44; within-family gains ranged from about threefold for T5 to under 20% for LLaMA over a ninefold size increase.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report improved factual-knowledge generation with larger OPT models in the tested relation subsets, and Table 2 reports increasing KaRR scores across the 7B, 13B, and 65B original LLaMA entries (r10, r13, r18, r21-r26).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the evaluated model families and tuning comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The paper says scaling benefits vary across models; same-size LLaMA variants have differing KaRR scores, with Alpaca lower and Vicuna higher than original 13B LLaMA (r13-r15).
